4Prompt structure levels
  1. Level 1Direct

    A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

  2. Level 2Structured

    Makes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.

  3. Level 3Specified

    Adds contract, boundaries, verification and definition of done.

  4. Level 4Orchestrated

    Separates system instructions from the user assignment for reuse.

MetodologIA

The library lets you compare four levels of structure and choose the minimum your task needs.

Start with your goal, add context and sources, and ask for evidence before expanding the instruction.

Keep the prompt, response, reviewed sources and the change you made after checking them.

10 working prompts

From a topic to defensible understanding

01
Learn

Research blueprint

Turn a broad topic into bounded research with an explicit in/out list and a sufficiency rule you can test.

Use it when
you need to understand a new topic before deciding or producing, and have no base built yet.
Example
Generative AI applied to my sales work, before choosing what to train in.
Output evidence
in/out scope list, essential questions, priority sources filtered by validity and region, named tensions and a testable sufficiency rule.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

I need to understand [TOPIC] to make [DECISION OR OUTCOME]. My context is [CONTEXT]. Bound the scope with an explicit in/out list; frame the essential questions; separate facts, interpretations and uncertainty. Prioritize primary sources with author, date, link and reason, filtered by validity within [TIME HORIZON] and applicability in [REGION OR JURISDICTION]; if those two constraints clash, ask me which one wins before continuing. Name the tensions between positions and the open gaps, and flag my risk of deciding on an incomplete base. If the topic is already narrow, validate the cut instead of narrowing it again. If no primary sources exist, declare coverage_gap and stop. Close with one testable sufficiency rule: a question I can answer for [AUDIENCE] without adjectives. Do not invent sources or certainty.

Level 2Structured

Level 4Orchestrated

Separates system instructions from the user assignment for reuse.

# systemResearch architect who bounds before searching# Guardrails- Never invent sources or certainty- No primary sources available: declare coverage_gap and stop- Topic already bounded: validate the cut, do not re-bound# Definition of DoneReviewable blueprint: explicit scope, every source with a reason and filter applied, and a sufficiency question answerable without adjectives.# user# InputsComplete or adjust values in brackets before running.# TaskTurn a broad topic into a bounded, testable blueprint for a personal decision# Workflow1. Record topic, personal decision, context and audience2. Bound the in/out scope or validate a cut already made3. Frame essential questions separating facts, interpretations and uncertainty4. Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The scope has an explicit in/out list
  • Every recommended source carries author, date, link and reason, and passes the validity and region filter
  • The sufficiency rule is a testable condition for the declared audience, not an adjective

Edge cases

  • Topic already bounded: the prompt validates the cut instead of destroying useful scope
  • No primary sources available: coverage_gap is declared instead of inventing

Trade-offs

  • Bounding trades coverage for verifiability

Assumptions

  • No base exists yet; if one does, 03 or 05 applies instead

Limits

  • It bounds the research, it does not run it
  • Accuracy is not guaranteed: the filter cuts noise, it does not validate source content
02
Learn

Source-grounded coach

Explains one idea per turn citing your base, asks you to restate it and corrects against the source, with a counterexample when the answer is shallow.

Use it when
you have sources and you want real understanding, not a summary.
Example
Understand RAG from my notes before a technical interview.
Output evidence
cited explanation with inference marked, one retrieval question per round, exact source to review and a close after three restatements without defined error.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Act as a learning coach on [TOPIC]. My base is [SOURCES OR NOTEBOOK]: state the mode and use it only. Cite every claim that carries a conclusion and mark it as cited evidence, your inference or missing data. Ask what I want to achieve with [DECISION OR DELIVERY] and what I think I know. Explain one idea per turn, ask me to restate it in my own words and correct: it is an error if my restatement contradicts the source or drops a condition it requires. If right but shallow, use a cited counterexample. If my question falls outside the base, say so; do not invent. If I miss the same idea twice, switch analogies. End each round with one retrieval question and the exact source. Finish when I restate three ideas in a row without error. Never grade my level: teach.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every explanation carrying a conclusion has a verifiable citation and is marked as evidence, inference or missing data
  • Each round closes with one retrieval question and the exact source
  • The session ends on three error-free restatements, where error means contradicting the source or dropping a condition it requires

Edge cases

  • Restatement right but shallow: a cited counterexample is used
  • Question outside the base: the limit is declared, nothing is answered from memory

Trade-offs

  • Slow pace — one idea per turn, plus counterexamples — in exchange for verifiable retention

Assumptions

  • A base with usage rights exists; in Notebook mode answers cite the loaded sources

Limits

  • It teaches; it never grades level: that belongs to the evaluator (08)
03
Learn

Deep research

Close one diagnosed gap with cited research, without uncontrolled scope growth.

Use it when
a previous audit revealed the gap blocking your outcome.
Example
Check the legal limits of using my chat logs as study material.
Output evidence
cited report answering the gap, a confidence scale declared up front and residual risk with a testable closing condition.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

I need to close the diagnosed gap [GAP], because it blocks [DECISION AT STAKE]. My acceptance criterion is [ACCEPTANCE CRITERION]. Research that gap only: in scope, the gap; out, any new topic. First fix the main question, the time and region of my case, the primary sources you accept, the minimum evidence per claim and the confidence scale (high, medium or low, defined). Deliver cited findings; a claim, evidence, confidence, limit table; contradictions with both sources; and residual risk with the testable condition that would close it. If public sources cannot close it, say: not provable within the given scope. If the gap mutates, restate the scope. If context on my case is missing, ask me up to three questions; if still missing, declare coverage_gap and do not invent certainty.

Confirm the diagnosed gap and the acceptance criterion2. Fix the main question, time and region bounds, accepted sources and minimum evidence3. Declare the confidence scale and the closed scope4. Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every claim in the table carries cited evidence, meets the minimum evidence and states confidence on the declared scale
  • Contradictions are listed with both sources
  • Residual risk is named together with the testable condition that would close it

Edge cases

  • Gap unclosable with public sources: explicit verdict of not provable within the given scope
  • The gap mutates during research: the scope is restated before continuing

Trade-offs

  • Depth on a single gap in exchange for not expanding coverage

Assumptions

  • A previous audit (05/W02) named the gap

Limits

  • It does not re-bound the whole topic: that is 01
  • It opens no new topics and does not guarantee the accuracy of cited sources
04
Learn

Claim cross-check

Verify a claim before you use it as a foundation, with an independent-origin threshold set by the risk of your use.

Use it when
you need to rest a decision on one concrete fact and its evidence is still uncertain.
Example
Confirm that an AI feature exists in the plan I am about to buy.
Output evidence
CONFIRMED, REFUTED or NOT DEMONSTRABLE verdict with origins counted, threshold applied and the demonstrable evidence that would change it.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

I want to verify [CLAIM] before I use it in [USE]. Count origins, not links: a chain from one origin is one source. Record per origin author, date, link, excerpt and limitation. CONFIRMED: two independent origins agree. REFUTED: one contradicts. Otherwise NOT DEMONSTRABLE, or [CLAIM] unverifiable by design. Require three origins when [USE] risks my money, my deadline or my reputation, or when it is blank. Split a mixed claim: one demonstrable verdict per part. Close with the evidence that would change the verdict and what I must not assert. Do not audit the base or rule on retention. Never invent sources or certainty.
2Level 2 · StructuredMakes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.
Level 2Structured

Makes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.

# Parametersunit = one atomic, datable claim per runindependence = a citation chain leading back to one origin counts as a single sourcethreshold = two independent origins; three when the use puts money, deadline or reputation at stakemissing_use = if the use is not stated, the high threshold applies# InputsComplete or adjust values in brackets before running.# TaskIssue a traceable verdict on one atomic claim before it supports a personal decision# Workflow1. Record the claim and the use it is meant for2. Trace every citation back to its origin and count origins, not links3. Record per origin author, date, link, excerpt and limitation4. Apply the threshold matching the stated use, or the high one if it is missing5. Issue CONFIRMED, REFUTED or NOT DEMONSTRABLE and name the evidence that would change it# Guardrails- Never invent sources or certainty- Citation chain with a single origin: count it as one source, not as corroboration- Do not audit the whole base or decide what to retain, update or remove: that is 05# Expected output- Per-origin record with author, date, link, excerpt and limitation- One verdict among CONFIRMED, REFUTED and NOT DEMONSTRABLE with the threshold applied- The concrete missing evidence that would change the verdict

Issue CONFIRMED, REFUTED or NOT DEMONSTRABLE and name the evidence that would change it# Expected output- Per-origin record with author, date, link, excerpt and limitation- One verdict among CONFIRMED, REFUTED and NOT DEMONSTRABLE with the threshold applied- The concrete missing evidence that would change the verdict
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The verdict is exactly one of CONFIRMED, REFUTED or NOT DEMONSTRABLE, and a reader can recount the cited origins and reproduce it
  • CONFIRMED appears only when the text shows two origins with different authors and links that do not lead back to the same publication; three when the stated use puts money, deadline or reputation at stake
  • "What would change the verdict" names one concrete, findable missing document or datum, not a generic call for better evidence

Edge cases

  • Citation chain with one origin: counts as a single source and does not unlock CONFIRMED
  • Mixed claim: split before verifying, each part gets its own verdict
  • Claim unverifiable by design: NOT DEMONSTRABLE with the reason stated

Trade-offs

  • The two-origin threshold makes the verdict conservative: fewer false CONFIRMED, more NOT DEMONSTRABLE
  • The frozen text asked to "prioritize the original source" as a preference; here it becomes origin counting, which absorbs it and makes it checkable

Assumptions

  • The claim is atomic and datable; if it arrives mixed, the prompt splits it

Limits

  • It verifies one claim; it does not audit a whole base or issue a sufficiency verdict: that is 05
  • Accuracy is not guaranteed: origin counting measures independence, not truth
05
Embody

Relevance audit of my base

Decide what to retain, update or remove from your learning base and whether it still meets your purpose.

Use it when
your library has grown and you need to know whether it still serves the purpose you built it for.
Example
Review the 20 sources in my Notebook before preparing a class.
Output evidence
retain, update or remove matrix with evidence per source, prioritized gaps and a sufficiency verdict naming the dimension that decided it.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Audit [BASE] against my purpose [PURPOSE]. Assess: usage rights and freshness block; authority and coverage decide; redundancy, bias, contradictions adjust. Ask licence or origin per source; without it, remove. Deliver a short summary and a source | retain, update, remove | evidence | impact | action table. Prioritize the gaps that block my purpose. Verdict BASE SUFFICIENT only if none blocks; else REPEAT RESEARCH; name the deciding dimension. If all is redundant, repeat anyway. With a multi-purpose [BASE], audit only against [PURPOSE]; if blank, ask me. Do not write assistant instruction or starter prompts, nor verify single claims. Never invent sources or certainty.
2Level 2 · StructuredMakes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.
Level 2Structured

Makes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.

Record the base and the single purpose it is audited against2. Ask for licence or origin per source before judging usage rights3. Assess the seven dimensions in the stated order of weight4. Decide retain, update or remove per source with the evidence for the decision5. Prioritize gaps and issue the verdict naming the dimension that decided it# Guardrails- Never invent sources or certainty- Source with no licence or known origin: remove by default, do not keep it just in case- Do not verify claims one by one or issue a verdict on a claim: that is 04- Do not write the assistant instruction, limits or starter prompts: that is 07# Expected output- Short summary of the state of the base- Table of source, decision, evidence for the decision, impact and action- Prioritized gaps and a sufficiency verdict with the deciding dimension

# systemRelevance auditor who decides source by source against a single purpose# Guardrails- Never invent sources or certainty- Source with no licence or known origin: remove by default, do not keep it just in case- Do not verify claims one by one or issue a verdict on a claim: that is 04- Do not write the assistant instruction, limits or starter prompts: that is 07# Definition of DoneEvery source carries a decision and its evidence, gaps are ordered by how far they block the purpose, and the verdict names the deciding dimension.# user# InputsComplete or adjust values in brackets before running.# TaskDecide what to retain, update or remove and issue a sufficiency verdict attributable to one dimension# Workflow1. Record the base and the single purpose it is audited against2. Ask for licence or origin per source before judging usage rights3. Assess the seven dimensions in the stated order of weight4. Decide retain, update or remove per source with the evidence for the decision5. Prioritize gaps and issue the verdict naming the dimension that decided it# Expected output- Short summary of the state of the base- Table of source, decision, evidence for the decision, impact and action- Prioritized gaps and a sufficiency verdict with the deciding dimension
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • No row is left undecided: every source comes out as retain, update or remove, with the evidence behind that decision cited in the same row
  • The verdict names the dimension that decided it, and a reader can return to the table and find the row holding it up
  • BASE SUFFICIENT appears only when no prioritized gap blocks the stated purpose; "sufficient" here means exactly that and never a judgement of volume

Edge cases

  • Ambiguous or missing purpose: the prompt asks for it instead of assuming it
  • High-volume base where everything is redundant: REPEAT RESEARCH
  • Source with no licence or origin: removed by default

Trade-offs

  • Removing sources cuts apparent coverage in exchange for signal per retained source
  • The frozen text closed with the slogan "do not reward volume"; it is replaced by a verdict tied to gaps, which actually prevents keeping everything

Assumptions

  • The purpose is single; a multi-purpose base is audited once per purpose

Limits

  • It audits sources; it does not verify one claim or issue its verdict: that is 04
  • It does not configure assistant behaviour or write its instruction and starter prompts: that is 07
  • Accuracy is not guaranteed: it decides relevance against the purpose, not truth of content

Never invent examples and never grade a demonstrated level.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • A third party with the same source compares my answer against the cited expected answer and decides hit or miss without personal judgment
  • The four activities arrive one at a time and none reveals the solution before my attempt
  • The new case marks which elements come from the base and which are invented scenario, and correction touches concepts only

Edge cases

  • Base without applicable examples: the practice shrinks to retrieval and explanation and says so
  • Failed retrieval: the activity is repeated instead of advancing to the next moment

Trade-offs

Limits

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The matrix leaves no loose findings: every row has evidence findable inside the Notebook, a named risk and an executable correction
  • The three adversarial tests appear with their results under a single pass criterion: the assistant states the limit instead of answering
  • The recommended configuration arrives marked as input and carries the explicit list of tasks forbidden with this base

Edge cases

  • Notebook with no declared purpose: the audit stops and asks for it
  • Doubtful rights: removed by default rather than kept pending clarification
  • Privacy compromised in one fragment: it is redacted or isolated and the chosen action is stated

Trade-offs

  • Auditing the container rather than each source loses relevance granularity, recovered by running 05 first
  • The frozen text asked for "sources to add or remove" as a decision of its own; here it surfaces only as a container coverage gap and the per-source decision stays in 05
  • The frozen "duplicates" dimension leaves the prompt: duplication is per-source relevance and is decided in 05; here it counts only when it opens a container gap

Assumptions

  • An operational Notebook exists with sources already loaded

Limits

  • It audits the container and its behaviour; it does not re-decide relevance source by source or issue a sufficiency verdict: that is 05
  • The configuration is a recommendation and authorizes neither publication nor use of the assistant

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every answer receives exactly one of the three levels together with the source quote that justifies it; another reviewer with that source reaches the same level
  • Dimension progression happens only on demonstrated, and the pass threshold — demonstrated in foundations and relationships — is declared before the first question
  • The final report gives level per dimension, its quote and a corrective practice, without comparing my performance to any other person

Edge cases

  • Partially correct answer: scored per dimension instead of passing or failing as a block
  • Answer brought from outside the base: flagged without penalty and excluded from the score

Trade-offs

  • Strengths and sources-to-revisit are lost as separate outputs from the frozen text: they are absorbed into the level per dimension with its supporting quote
  • One question at a time lengthens the session in exchange for a clean per-dimension diagnosis

Assumptions

  • The declared base covers the four dimensions; otherwise the dimension is declared unassessable

Limits

  • It measures level; it neither teaches nor accompanies understanding: that belongs to the coach (02)
  • It does not guarantee content accuracy: the level measures agreement with the source, not the truth of the source

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every objection names a concrete risk of the topic and its difficulty rises only if the previous answer quoted the base and answered the objection
  • Honest is defined inside the session: declaring the limit without backing scores a hit and claiming without backing scores a miss; it is not an adjective
  • The three rewritten answers quote the declared base and a third party can check each quote against it

Edge cases

  • Collapse on the first question: difficulty drops one level before continuing
  • Honest answer is I do not know: the limit declaration scores as a hit, not a miss

Trade-offs

  • The frozen text ran adversarial objections with no quotable base: [SOURCES] is added as a mandatory base and the simulation does not start without it
  • Three frozen variables are lost —[INTERVIEW, QBR OR DEFENCE], [AUDIENCE] and [OUTCOME]—: the format stays literal in the first sentence and the calibrated difficulty level replaces the audience profile
  • The strengths section of the frozen closing does not survive: the 2x budget only covers critical gaps and the three rewritten answers, which are the actionable output
  • The explicit log of the difficulty drop leaves the prompt under the 2x budget and remains a session criterion
  • Rising pressure in exchange for an uncomfortable but diagnostic session

Assumptions

  • The content to defend already exists; otherwise the simulation stops and routes to 10

Limits

  • It tests the argument; it neither drafts, restructures nor builds narrative: that belongs to the preparer (10)
  • It measures the defence, not the truth of the content: surviving pressure does not validate the thesis

Build the narrative that does not exist yet: a one-sentence thesis, three cited ideas, a structure in timed blocks and rehearsal after your confirmation.

Use it when
you must present what you learned and you have no script or structure yet.
Example
Prepare my eight-minute talk on AI opportunities and limits.
Output evidence
one-sentence thesis, structure with minutes per block, speaker notes, and five likely questions with cited answers after the rehearsal.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Help me build a presentation on [TOPIC] in [TIME] from [SOURCES]. If the script exists, stop: this builds, not tests. One-sentence thesis, then three ideas, each with a literal [SOURCES] quote, plus limit and call. Split [TIME] into timed blocks summing to the total; if three do not fit, cut one, named. No quote for an idea: declare a hypothesis or drop it. Ask if my audience is hostile or neutral; tune tension. Concise visual structure: one idea per block, no text read aloud, plus my speaker notes. After my yes, rehearse by section, challenge weak claims, then five likely [TOPIC] questions, cited. No rising-pressure interrogation, no scoring, no invented quotes.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The thesis fits in one sentence and each of the three ideas carries a literal quote from the declared base
  • The structure blocks carry minutes adding to the declared time; if an idea is cut, the script says which and why
  • Concise is defined here: one idea per block and no text the speaker must read aloud
  • Rehearsal does not start until my explicit confirmation of the script

Edge cases

  • Idea without an available quote: downgraded to a declared hypothesis or dropped, never padded
  • Hostile versus neutral audience: tension and call to action change, the quotes do not

Trade-offs

  • The frozen variables [AUDIENCE] and [OUTCOME] are lost: the audience stance is asked in session to free budget
  • The tension of the frozen text survives as audience-stance tuning in persona and as the named operational risk in empresa
  • A shorter cited script in exchange for less rhetorical effect

Assumptions

  • Understanding of the topic already exists; otherwise stepping back to 01-08 applies

Limits

  • It rehearses sections; it neither simulates rising adversarial interrogation nor scores under pressure: that belongs to the simulator (09)
  • It prepares the script; it does not guarantee the audience decision
4 meta-prompts

Build instruments for continued learning

M1
Meta-prompt

Learning coach generator

Design the instrument, not the session: a reusable coach system prompt with diagnostic questions, declared limits and tests that try to induce invention.

Use it when
you want to reuse your method on another topic or audience and you need the coach as a part, not a class.
Example
Cybersecurity coach for non-technical leaders, built on my notes from last quarter's course.
Output evidence
coach system prompt with role, base, flow and opening message, five diagnostic questions, declared limits and three adversarial tests with the correct answer.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Design a learning coach on [TOPIC] for [AUDIENCE] with [SOURCES] as my only source base: I want the instrument, not the session. Do not explain [TOPIC] or correct restatements. Deliver a reusable system prompt with role, base, turn flow and the opening message of my first session; five diagnostic questions that change if [AUDIENCE] is new or expert, and if it mixes levels, design for the newest. In the limits write that the coach never issues a level, score, verdict or grading rubric. If [SOURCES] do not cover [TOPIC], the coach opens by declaring coverage_gap instead of filling. Close with three adversarial tests: the attack that tries to induce invention and the correct answer, which is to declare the limit. Never promise the coach cannot fail.

Level 2Structured

Makes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The system prompt carries role, base, flow, limits and opening message, none of them empty
  • Each adversarial test names the attack and the expected correct answer, which is to declare the limit
  • The limits state in writing that no level, score or verdict may be issued
  • The output contains no explanation of the topic: if it does, the request was 02

Edge cases

  • Mixed audience: the prompt fixes the rule (design for the newest) rather than leaving it to the model
  • Insufficient sources: the generated coach opens with coverage_gap instead of filling

Trade-offs

  • The coach stays bounded to the base in exchange for traceable answers
  • Designing the instrument costs a turn that a direct 02 session does not charge
  • «Three tests proving it does not invent» becomes «three attacks with a correct answer»: the promise is lost, an executable test is gained

Assumptions

  • Whoever uses the coach will keep the base up to date
  • The declared audience matches whoever will actually use the coach

Limits

  • It generates the instrument, it does not run the session: teaching the topic is 02
  • It issues no level, score or verdict: measuring is M2
  • It does not guarantee the coach will never fail: tests document answers, they do not prove absence of invention
M2
Meta-prompt

Progressive evaluator generator

Design the measuring instrument, not the measurement: an observable rubric with three named levels, an eight-task bank and explicit advance and retry rules.

Use it when
you need to test your mastery on another topic and want a reusable evaluator, not a one-off session.
Example
Safe-AI-use evaluator to measure my own mastery before applying it in a real case.
Output evidence
evaluator system prompt, observable rubric of three levels with the evidence each one demands, eight graded tasks, advance rule, retry rule and a final report per dimension.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Design an evaluator for [TOPIC] from [SOURCES]: I want the instrument to measure my mastery, not to be assessed now. Deliver its system prompt with an observable rubric: absent if no [SOURCES] condition is quoted, partial if a required one is dropped, demonstrated if quoted verbatim. Eight [TOPIC] tasks, two per level: retrieval, explanation, application, transfer. Advance only on demonstrated; one retry replaces the result. It corrects by quoting, never teaches or uses analogies and never reveals the answer before my attempt. Task uncovered by [SOURCES]: dropped, never invented. A hit from outside the base is logged unscored. Compare runs against the rubric, never people.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The rubric names three levels and each declares its observable evidence: no condition quoted, a required condition dropped, verbatim reproduction
  • The eight tasks map two by two to retrieval, explanation, application and transfer
  • Advance and retry rules state the maximum and the effect on the result, with no adjectives
  • The instrument contains no comparison between people

Edge cases

  • Base missing a cognitive level: it is declared and the bank drops below eight tasks instead of inventing them
  • A hit from outside knowledge: logged unscored, because measurement runs against the base

Trade-offs

  • Narrow, base-only measurement in exchange for a verdict defensible by quote
  • «Eight graded tasks» with no stated dimension becomes two tasks per cognitive level: grading freedom is lost, an auditable bank is gained

Assumptions

  • The base covers the four cognitive levels; otherwise the bank shrinks and says so

Limits

  • It generates the instrument, it does not run the assessment: measuring is 08
  • It does not teach: explaining, restating and counterexamples are M1
  • The measured level describes the answer against the base, not the person's capability
M3
Meta-prompt

Adversarial interviewer generator

Design the instrument, not the conversation: an interviewer with traceable objections, a declared maximum branch depth and a four-criterion observable rubric.

Use it when
your argument already exists and you want a reusable interviewer that presses it, not a one-off session.
Example
Interviewer to defend my architecture before a security panel, with cost and alternative objections.
Output evidence
interviewer system prompt, objection map traced to evidence or risk, maximum branch depth, rubric of clarity, grounding, judgment and honesty, and a feedback format.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Design an interviewer for [SCENARIO] before [AUDIENCE] with [SOURCES]: I want the instrument, not the interview. If [SOURCES] cannot sustain objections to my thesis, reduce the map and declare the gap. Deliver its system prompt, a ten-question map tuned to [AUDIENCE], branch depth capped at two, and a rubric of clarity, grounding, judgment and honesty, each with its observable evidence. Every objection traces to a [SOURCES] quote or a declared [SCENARIO] risk; untraced, it is dropped. Limits: it never drafts or restructures my deliverable and never imitates identifiable real people, it uses an archetype. Do not invent objections.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every objection traces to a base quote or a declared scenario risk, and untraceable ones are dropped
  • Branching declares a depth cap of two, so the whole map can be run end to end
  • Each rubric criterion states what is observed: declaring a limit with backing is a hit, claiming it without backing is a miss
  • The instrument contains no drafted fragment of the deliverable

Edge cases

  • Base too thin to sustain objections: a reduced map is delivered and the gap declared before generating
  • Identifiable real person: the instrument substitutes an archetype instead of imitating them

Trade-offs

  • A capped map loses combinatorics in exchange for being runnable end to end
  • «Realistic objections» with no source of realism becomes traced objections: spontaneity is lost, verifiability is gained

Assumptions

  • Whoever uses the instrument already has a written argument to defend; if not, M4 or 10 applies

Limits

  • It generates the simulator, it does not run the session: interviewing is 09
  • It neither prepares nor drafts the deliverable: building narrative and rehearsing is M4
  • Simulated pressure does not predict how a real audience will react
M4
Meta-prompt

Delivery preparer generator

Design the instrument, not the deliverable: a preparer with observable gates, a template branched by delivery type and a quality checklist.

Use it when
your deliverable does not exist yet and you want a reusable preparer, not someone writing your script.
Example
Masterclass preparer for my talk to operations leaders, inside a fixed slot.
Output evidence
preparer system prompt, preparation flow with gates, template per delivery type, quality checklist, rehearsal in parts and a ready-or-coverage_gap verdict.

Branch the template by [DELIVERABLE] type —talk, class, memo, decision; if missing, ask first. Define transfer as [AUDIENCE] being able to act on what is delivered. Add a quality checklist. If time is short for [TOPIC], it cuts scope first; evidence without rights is excluded and declared. Limits: no rising-pressure interrogation, no invented quotes.

# SPEC MetodologIAversion: 2.0status: executable## S — SituationContext: your deliverable does not exist yet and you want a reusable preparer, not someone writing your script.Reference case: Masterclass preparer for my talk to operations leaders, inside a fixed slot.# InputsComplete or adjust values in brackets before running.## P — RequestExpert role: Specialist in evidence-grounded learning and researchDeliverable: preparer system prompt, preparation flow with gates, template per delivery type, quality checklist, rehearsal in parts and a ready-or-coverage_gap verdict.Scope includes: Design the instrument, not the deliverable: a preparer with observable gates, a template branched by delivery type and a quality checklist.Scope excludes: claims without provenance, unavailable capabilities, or decisions that belong to the person## E — ExecutionSteps:1. Record delivery type, topic, audience and base as instrument configuration, not as a script to write2. Write the preparer system prompt and its observable gates in order3. Branch the template by delivery type and ask for the type when missing4. Define transfer observably and add the quality checklist5. Close with the ready-or-coverage_gap criterion and the time-based scope-cut rule6. Check provenance, boundaries, and consistency before delivery.7. Return only the final result and closing metadata.### Edge cases- If material information is missing, ask up to three concrete questions before continuing.- If sources conflict, surface the tension and do not force a conclusion.- If evidence is insufficient, declare coverage_gap and state what would close it.## C — CriterionOutput:- Preparer system prompt with its gates in order- Template branched by delivery type and a quality checklist- Ready-or-coverage_gap criterion and the time-based scope-cut ruleObservable acceptance criteria:- The result answers the purpose and respects the declared scope.- Every material claim links to a source or is marked as inference, assumption, or gap.- Boundaries, confidence, and the next verifiable step are explicit.Definition of Done: A third party can run the prompt in one step and inspect the result, its provenance, and its boundaries.## Provenance tags- [SOURCE] verifiable evidence- [INFERENCE] derived conclusion- [ASSUMPTION] unconfirmed information- [GAP] missing evidence## Closing metadata- sources used- active assumptions- coverage_gaps- global confidence from 0.0 to 1.0Do not request or expose private reasoning or chain of thought; return only conclusions, evidence, and auditable metadata.

# systemDelivery-preparer designer: builds the instrument, not the script# Guardrails- Never invent quotes, evidence or usage rights- Never write the deliverable or its sections: that is 10- The generated preparer applies no rising adversarial pressure and grades nothing under pressure: that is M3- Evidence without usage rights: excluded and declared# Definition of DoneReviewable instrument: every gate states what is observed to call it passed, the template has one branch per delivery type and the ready criterion is testable.# user# InputsComplete or adjust values in brackets before running.# TaskProduce a reusable preparer with observable gates, a template branched by type and a quality checklist# Workflow1. Record delivery type, topic, audience and base as instrument configuration, not as a script to write2. Write the preparer system prompt and its observable gates in order3. Branch the template by delivery type and ask for the type when missing4. Define transfer observably and add the quality checklist5. Close with the ready-or-coverage_gap criterion and the time-based scope-cut rule# Expected output- Preparer system prompt with its gates in order- Template branched by delivery type and a quality checklist- Ready-or-coverage_gap criterion and the time-based scope-cut rule
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The flow has five gates and each states what is observed to call it passed, with no adjectives
  • The template carries one branch per delivery type, or an explicit single-type assumption
  • Transfer is defined as the audience being able to act on what is delivered, with the evidence that shows it
  • The instrument contains no drafted section of the deliverable

Edge cases

  • Missing delivery type: it is requested before generating, instead of assuming a talk
  • Insufficient time: the scope cut happens before preparing, not during rehearsal

Trade-offs

  • A strict checklist costs creative flexibility in exchange for a testable ready criterion
  • The six variables of the base text drop to four required ones: time and outcome are asked inside the purpose gate, in exchange for every declared variable being consumed at least twice
  • «Check transfer» becomes «the audience can act on what is delivered»: breadth is lost, an observable criterion is gained

Assumptions

  • The sources were audited before preparing; if not, 05 or 07 applies

Limits

  • It generates the instrument, it neither builds nor rehearses the actual delivery: that is 10
  • It applies no rising adversarial pressure and grades nothing under pressure: that is M3 and 09
  • The ready criterion describes the preparation, it does not predict the outcome with a real audience

Derived from the open Learn · Embody · (R)Evolve skill. Answers must remain tied to sources, boundaries and human judgment.
